attempted.title: JavaScript: expose provenance-preserving categorical evidence assessment for legal reasoning
attempted.body:
The JavaScript relative meta-logic component at fd5bfaced85262a51b341fb2b25c79e507423ca3 aggregates probabilistic evidence, but legal source absence, contradictions and contextual applicability need an explicit categorical interface.

Downstream work: https://github.com/link-assistant/legal/pull/2 (issue https://github.com/link-assistant/legal/issues/1).

Proposed addition: assessLegalContext(evidence) returning supported / contradicted / conflict / unknown, with provenance labels. Empty input must remain unknown; opposing source stances must remain a conflict. A probability must not be presented as proof of legal validity.

We are developing a patch against js/agentic/crate/relative_meta_logic.mjs in the downstream PR, kept as a patch with the pinned source checksum, and deterministic tests for exceptions, missing facts, dates, jurisdiction, conflicting rules and source drift. Executable rules require reviewed semantics and exact source spans. Surface modal extraction is explicitly unverified. This does not claim to solve arbitrary legal reasoning.

Upstream incorporation would remove the temporary patch and support other deterministic applications. Broader automatic semantic formalization of legislation remains an unresolved capability requirement.

attempted.title: 0.354.1 loops for 4.5 h at 100% CPU via Codex: pushes to branch 'so' (a word from the prompt), then calls web_run with {} 119 times (wrong 'query' key, no repeat stop)
attempted.body:
## What happened

On 2026-10-20 a Hive Mind run, `solve https://github.com/konard/test-hello-world-019fb331-c107-78c7-8ff6-9f127a3c593c/issues/1 --tool codex --model formal-ai`, kept the Formal AI sidecar at **100% of one CPU core for more than 6 hours** (08:27 → still looping at 14:50 UTC) and produced nothing. It was not stopped, so the loop can be watched live. Restarting the sidecar does not end it (see the "Restart test" section below).

Formal AI did the real work in the first 13 minutes, then spent hours doing nothing useful:

| Time (UTC) | Codex item | What Formal AI did | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 08:29 | item_1 | `gh issue view … --json title`, `… --json body` | ok |
| 08:31–08:33 | item_3, item_5 | added `main.rs`, `tests/verify-output.sh` | ok |
| 08:35 | item_7 | `rustc main.rs -o main` | exit 0 |
| 08:37 | item_9 | `sh tests/verify-output.sh` | `Hello, World!` |
| 08:41:51 | item_11 | `git add … && git commit … && git push -q origin 'so' && git rev-parse HEAD` | **`error: src refspec so does not match any`**, exit 1 |
| 08:44 → now | item_12 … item_249 | "Let me search the web for rust src refspec so does not match any." plus `codex_apps` MCP tool `search_service.web_run` with **`arguments: {}`** | **161 times by 14:40 UTC** (and counting) the same `InvalidActionArgumentsError: Provide either an input string or top-level Search commands, without combining them.` (`error_code INVALID_ACTION_ARGUMENTS`, `failure_stage argument_binding`) |

All of it is one Codex turn (`turn.started` once, never completed). The branch Hive Mind had checked out and named in its prompt was `issue-1-09b0c76bd0e4` (PR #2). The commit `feat: add main.rs` exists only in the task container; nothing was pushed. The issue also asks for a GitHub Actions workflow, which was never started.

## Root cause

Code references are at `v0.354.1`. Each item says whether `v0.355.0` changes it.

**1. "so" is taken as the branch name** (`rust/src/agentic_coding/git_commit.rs:48-67`). `named_branch` walks word pairs of the whole request and returns the first word after a `git_branch_cue` surface ("branch") that passes `is_branch_name`. Hive Mind's Codex prompt says (`src/codex.prompts.lib.mjs:206`):

> commit each atomic step that is useful on its own to the pull request **branch so** interrupted work remains preserved in the pull request.

That gives the pair `("branch", "so")`. `"so"` is a legal ref name, so `CommitTarget::push_ref()` (`:32`) plans `git push -q origin 'so'`. The branch Hive Mind had already checked out (`issue-1-09b0c76bd0e4`) is never asked from git. *0.355.0 rewrites `named_branch` with `branch-binding-patterns` and a `branch-forbidden-substrings` policy, which should reject this word. It still reads the branch from prose, not from `git branch --show-current`.*

**2. `web_run` is called with the wrong argument key** (`rust/src/agentic_coding/repair_loop.rs:741-746`). After the failed push, `repair_step` (the E149 / #1185 error-driven repair loop) plans a search for the error:

```rust
if progress.search_output.is_none() {
    let Some(tool) = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Search) else { … };
    let query = search_query(&failure.language, primary);
    return RepairOutcome::Search(plan_one(tool, json!({ "query": query }).to_string()));
}
```

The key is always `"query"`, whatever the tool's JSON schema says. Codex's `codex_apps` / `search_service.web_run` takes `input`, so Codex binds nothing and sends `{}`. The tool answers `InvalidActionArgumentsError` (`failure_stage: argument_binding`). The search text itself was reasonable ("rust src refspec so does not match any"). *Unchanged in 0.355.0.*

**3. Nothing ever stops the repeat.** Three guards exist, and none fires:
- **Search never counts as done.** `Progress::scan` (`progress.rs:157-163`) sets `search_output` only from a non-empty normalized payload of a `Capability::Search` result. The error result evidently never sets it (otherwise the next step would have been a fetch), so `repair_step:741` plans the search again on every turn.
- **The repair rung never advances.** `MAX_REPAIR_RUNGS = 3` (`repair_loop.rs:74`) bounds the repair ladder, but only a failed `Capability::Run` step advances a rung. A failed search does not, so the ladder stays at rung 0.
- **Identical failures are not counted.** `stop_repeated_failure` (`planner/steps.rs:48`) needs `identical_failures_of(tool) >= 2` (`progress.rs:431`), and `stop_repeated_call` (`steps.rs:17`) needs an earlier successful identical call. Neither condition was met in 119 identical failed calls; the most likely reason is that this MCP error result is not recorded as a failure (inference).

*0.355.0 changes the evidence window of `stop_repeated_call` / `stop_repeated_failure` (`repetition_progress`) but not the search, rung or failure-classification paths.* This is the same family as #1154: a progress check that does not recognise the client's own tool result shape.

**4. About 130 s of a full core per request.** The cause below is an inference from code reading; the profile after it is measured. On turn 1 the whole Hive Mind context is a single user message, so the chat "prompt" is the full 277 KB. `normalize_prompt` (`engine.rs:668`) lower-cases it, rewrites it character by character, re-joins the tokens and runs `expand_contractions` over every token. It is not memoized, and it runs again for each solver path (`solver.rs` around 460, 583, 656) and for each handler check (`rule_interpreter.rs:464` → `Context` at `:614`). That is roughly 20 full passes per request over a text that is mostly the same on every turn. *Unchanged in 0.355.0.*

Profile (measured: `perf record -F 199 -g -p <pid> -- sleep 20`, 3,924 samples, 14:40 UTC). The binary is stripped, so only addresses are available. With your unstripped build of the same binary (`/usr/local/bin/formal-ai` 0.354.1, GNU BuildID `7ca72067f887b5ce6bd745634c3a31d37344638f`, sha256 `db0fb0598d418178843bab162b845f246fd81c1251444b731172acaf6ce79ded`), `addr2line -f -C -i -e formal-ai <address>` names them:

| Self time | File offset |
|---|---|
| 42% in total | one ~12 KB code region, `0xe2f2979`–`0xe2f5840` (hottest: `0xe2f2a4d` 5.8%, `0xe2f2b92` 4.0%, `0xe2f2979` 2.4%, `0xe2f2982` 1.9%, `0xe2f2a43` 1.7%, `0xe2f2999` 1.7%, `0xe2f5840` 1.7%) |
| 1.5% | `0xf5836e4` |
| ~20% inclusive (6.3% self) | `malloc`, `free`, `realloc` |

One tight loop plus heavy allocation fits a per-character string rewrite that is repeated over a large text, but that it is `normalize_prompt` is still to be confirmed with the symbols. Two `formal-ai-conne` threads had used 58 and 34 CPU-minutes.

## Restart test

To check whether a restart is a workaround, the sidecar was restarted with all logs collected first: `docker restart -t 10 hive-mind-formal-ai` at 14:44:53 UTC, the same container, image and arguments, `/health` ok at 14:45:12 (0.354.1).

- **Codex (this task) continued the same turn and the same loop at once.** It logged `retry: stream connection failed; waiting to retry … retry_delay=5s`, resent the conversation (434,224 B) at 14:45:14, and the answer was again `search_service.web_run` with `{}` → `InvalidActionArgumentsError`. The next requests followed at 14:47:33 and 14:49:47, about 135 s apart, at 100% of a core as before.
- So the loop does not live in the server's memory. The plan is a function of the conversation alone: the same transcript always gives the same `web_run {}`. A restart costs the client one retry and changes nothing, so it is **not** a workaround. Only a new plan for this transcript (Root cause 1–3) or ending the session stops it.
- A second client, `solve …/test-hello-world-019fb330-…/issues/1 --tool agent --model formal-ai` (it was making progress), got `ECONNREFUSED` at 14:45:07 during the restart. Hive Mind treated it as a transient network failure and resumed the preserved session at 14:51:15 (the sidecar was back after 19 s, but that retry waits a fixed 6 minutes). Neither client lost work. At 14:53 UTC both were still running: the agent task went on working (23 tool calls before the restart, 30 after), and the Codex task went on looping (4 more identical requests).

## Cost

Each Codex request takes Formal AI **121–144 s of 100% of one core**, from the first turn on:

| Request | Body | Answer after |
|---|---|---|
| 1 (08:29:05) | 277,529 B | 129.7 s |
| 6 (08:39:47) | 291,407 B | 123.4 s |
| 60 (10:35:14) | 338,320 B | 131.2 s |
| 124 (12:58:26) | 393,616 B | 143.5 s |
| 168 (14:37:39) | 431,632 B | 138 s to the next request |

The body grows by about 864 bytes per looping turn: one more identical message and failed call. Codex sends the next request as soon as an answer arrives, so the core never idles. `formal-ai serve` had used 262 CPU-minutes in 267 minutes of life when it was first sampled, and 374 CPU-minutes in 370 minutes at 14:38 UTC. On a 6-core host that also runs Claude and Codex tasks, the load average stayed at 6–9.

## No logs were persisted

The sidecar's volume `/home/box/.formal-ai` was owned by root (a Hive Mind deployment problem, reported in link-assistant/hive-mind#3583), so every exchange logged three errors and nothing reached disk:

- 381× `logging_failure` / `logging_failed_check_log_directory_permissions_and_space` (`reason file_write_failed`), the first at startup;
- about 124× `[dialog-log] failed to record exchange: Permission denied (os error 13)`;
- about 124× `[memory] failed to record live chat exchange: refusing to write an incompatible persisted-memory schema`. This is a misleading message for a directory that is empty and unwritable: there is no persisted schema to be incompatible with.

Formal AI's defaults were already the most detailed: `--verbose` is the default, and stdout carries `debug` records. But the records about a request only say `large_native_diagnostic` with the body size and a SHA-256. So the planner's decisions (why `so`, why `web_run`, why `{}`, why the same plan again) are not visible anywhere, even at debug level.

Where the two messages come from:

- `logging_failed_check_log_directory_permissions_and_space` is `structured_log.rs:317-331`. It is written once **per log event**, and the server goes on without logs. It never says which directory or which error (`Permission denied`).
- `refusing to write an incompatible persisted-memory schema` is `memory_sync.rs:432`. The store is marked `compatible = false` at `memory_sync.rs:274` when `synchronize_link_cli_projection()` fails. Here that is because the directory is not writable. The real error is printed **only when `FORMAL_AI_MEMORY_DEBUG` is set** (`:268-272`), which is off by default. So the default log names a schema problem that does not exist and hides the actual cause.

## Expected

1. **Push to the current branch.** The push target comes from `git branch --show-current` (or `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`) in the working directory, or from the branch Hive Mind's prompt names, never from a word in prose. A push that fails with `src refspec … does not match any` is repaired by re-reading the current branch, not by a web search.
2. **Bind tool arguments from the tool's schema, or do not call the tool.** `web_run` (Codex's `codex_apps` `search_service.web_run`) needs an `input` string. A call whose required arguments come out empty is never sent: it is a planning error, logged with the schema and the values that could not be bound.
3. **Detect no progress.** The same tool, the same arguments and the same error N times in a row (3 is plenty) is a loop. Change strategy, or end the session with an honest failure report that names the loop. The tool error text here (`Provide either an input string…`) is a direct instruction that the planner ignored 119 times.
4. **Bound the cost per request.** About 130 s of a full core for a 277 KB request, before any history, makes every coding session take hours. Most of the request is Codex's fixed instructions and tool definitions, which are the same on every turn and can be parsed or indexed once per session.
5. **Fail loudly when logs cannot be written.** At startup, if `FORMAL_AI_LOG_DIR` / `~/.formal-ai` is not writable, say so once, clearly, and expose it on `/health` (for example `"logs": "unwritable: Permission denied"`), so the host (Hive Mind) can warn or fix it instead of 381 identical records. Name the real cause in the memory error, and print the `synchronize_link_cli_projection` error by default instead of only under `FORMAL_AI_MEMORY_DEBUG`.
6. **Log the planner's decisions at debug level** (chosen action, tool, bound arguments, the progress or loop state), not only the body size and hash, so a loop like this can be explained from the log alone (#1220).

## Logs (private gists; the email and Codex/OpenAI account ids are redacted)

- Task log (Codex event stream, start-command, solve), 2026-10-20 08:27 → 14:40 UTC: https://gist.github.com/konard/43c9c883d4ab7bfb6b0fca20290a6a4d
- Formal AI sidecar stdout (`docker logs --timestamps hive-mind-formal-ai`), 08:27 → 14:40 UTC: https://gist.github.com/konard/0ac634fc4c62a3bbd13a02382e7d9ec4
- Codex rollout (`~/.codex/sessions/…/rollout-…-01a1586d-….jsonl`, 876 KB): the full conversation Codex sends to Formal AI on every turn, to replay the exact request: https://gist.github.com/konard/ca8e40df2a2b195ea84b93404427a0f0
- Earlier snapshots, up to 13:03 UTC: [task](https://gist.github.com/konard/c24e69645c4fd35e3b6f5b73e6fda4e1), [sidecar](https://gist.github.com/konard/59ce995cffb9a10165fbece3e60e4a9c)

## Versions

Formal AI 0.354.1 (sidecar image `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.39.2`, `formal-ai serve --agent-mode --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080`; latest release is 0.355.0), Codex CLI 0.163.0 (`codex exec`, `--model formal-ai`), Hive Mind 2.39.2. Codex conversation `01a1586d-a94a-7770-877b-2daebf8de380`, start-command execution `b8b78e59-8c3a-463d-a53b-3b274209a064`.

## Related

- #1162 (E118, Hello World via Hive Mind and Codex; this is one more failure of it), #1154 (E119, Codex re-plans the same read 78 times: the same family of no-progress loop), #1185 (E149, error-driven repair loop: here the "search the error" step runs, with no arguments and no stop), #1189 (words from prose taken as targets: "e.g." as a file, here "so" as a branch), #1211 (files named after words in the prompt), #1220 (debug logs by default).
- link-assistant/hive-mind#3048 (no default CPU limit for task containers; the sidecar has none either), link-assistant/hive-mind#2316 (the repeated-tool-call breaker exists only for Claude).

attempted.title: Detect that two questions have the same meaning with different wording (sameMeaning(a, b))
attempted.body:
# Feature request: `sameMeaning(a, b)` — detect that two questions have the same meaning with different wording

## Context

[meta-sovereign](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign) (a local, open-source messenger client) learns which questions were asked in a conversation and wants to treat questions with the same meaning but different wording as one (its requirement R-Y54). We tried the latest formal-ai locally for this; the examples below are synthetic.

## Summary

formal-ai has no API for comparing two arbitrary natural-language questions and deciding whether they convey the same intent. A `sameMeaning(a, b) -> { same: boolean, confidence: number }` function is needed, working for both Russian and English.

## Commit

`98f7808d49583e1e7932d133355445d8fdfb91f9` (default branch at time of evaluation)

## Environment

- OS: macOS Darwin 24.6.0 (arm64)
- Rust: 1.99.1 (58cf8f9c3 2026-10-13), installed via `rustup toolchain install 1.99`
- Node: v24.18.0
- formal-ai version: 0.355.0

## Exact commands

```bash
# build (one-time):
rustup toolchain install 1.99
rustup override set 1.99   # inside formal-ai repo
cargo +1.99 run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --bin formal-ai -- --help

# per-prompt test used:
cargo +1.99 run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --bin formal-ai -- \
  chat --prompt "На вы?" --format text --silent
```

No dedicated same-meaning endpoint exists. The evaluation ran each prompt individually via `chat` and compared the raw text outputs.

## Expected vs actual for each pair

| # | Prompt A | Prompt B | Expected | A response (summary) | B response (summary) | Result |
|---|----------|----------|----------|----------------------|----------------------|--------|
| 1 | "На вы?" | "Можно к вам на вы обращаться?" | same | lookup failure (no cached data for "На вы") | unknown rule | FAIL — routes to different handlers |
| 2 | "Можно на ты?" | "Давай на ты?" | same | lookup failure (topic "Можно") | lookup failure (topic "Давай") | FAIL — different lookup keys, same underlying intent ignored |
| 3 | "Where do you work?" | "What company are you at?" | same | lookup failure (no cached data) | self-identity response: "I am formal-ai…" | FAIL — completely different routes |
| 4 | "Кем ты работаешь?" | "Чем занимаешься по работе?" | same | unknown | unknown | FAIL — both unknown, equivalence not detected |
| 5 | "Do you have a LinkedIn?" | "Can you send me your LinkedIn profile?" | same | unknown | **misroutes to `list_dir`** capability | FAIL — wrong route on B; intent not recognised |
| 6 | "Когда созвонимся?" | "В какое время удобно поговорить?" | same | unknown | unknown | FAIL — both unknown, equivalence not detected |
| 7 | "На вы?" | "На ты?" | different | lookup failure "На вы" | lookup failure "На ты" | ACCIDENTAL PASS — different only because lookup keys differ, not due to semantic comparison |
| 8 | "Where do you work?" | "Where do you live?" | different | lookup failure "Where do you work" | lookup failure "Where do you live" | ACCIDENTAL PASS — same reason |
| 9 | "Когда созвонимся?" | "Зачем созваниваться?" | different | unknown | unknown | ACCIDENTAL PASS — both unknown; no semantic differentiation |

Summary: 0 of 9 pairs correctly handled by semantic reasoning. The 3 "different" pairs appear correct only by coincidence (the lookup key or the boilerplate intro differs); the system performs no actual equivalence comparison.

## Minimal reproduction

```bash
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai repo
cd repo
rustup toolchain install 1.99 && rustup override set 1.99
cargo +1.99 run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --bin formal-ai -- \
  chat --prompt "Where do you work?" --format text --silent
# → "No captured provider response is available for `Where do you work`."

cargo +1.99 run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --bin formal-ai -- \
  chat --prompt "What company are you at?" --format text --silent
# → "I am formal-ai, a deterministic symbolic AI implementation…"
```

These two questions mean the same thing but produce entirely different responses from different handlers.

A second sharp failure:

```bash
cargo +1.99 run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --bin formal-ai -- \
  chat --prompt "Can you send me your LinkedIn profile?" --format text --silent
# → "This request routes to the `list_dir` capability, but this chat surface does not expose the required `shell` tool."
```

"Can you send me your LinkedIn profile?" is wrongly routed to `list_dir`.

## What API would help

A deterministic, symbolic `sameMeaning(a, b)` function that:

1. Formalises both inputs into intent frames using the existing meanings lexicon
   (`rust/src/seed/meanings.rs`) and the multilingual cue lexicon
   (`rust/src/cue_lexicon.rs`).
2. Compares the resulting frames structurally — same intent type, same
   subject slot, compatible argument types.
3. Returns `{ same: bool, confidence: f64, intent_a: String, intent_b: String }`
   so the caller can inspect the reasoning.
4. Works for at least Russian and English (the two main languages in the
   existing test matrix).

Suggested Rust signature:

```rust
pub fn same_meaning(a: &str, b: &str) -> SameMeaningResult;

pub struct SameMeaningResult {
    pub same: bool,
    pub confidence: f64,   // 0.0–1.0
    pub intent_a: String,  // canonical intent label for `a`
    pub intent_b: String,  // canonical intent label for `b`
}
```

Suggested CLI surface:

```bash
formal-ai same-meaning --a "Where do you work?" --b "What company are you at?"
# → { "same": true, "confidence": 0.92, "intent_a": "ask_employer", "intent_b": "ask_employer" }
```

And a corresponding HTTP endpoint:

```
POST /api/openai/v1/same-meaning
{ "a": "...", "b": "..." }
→ { "same": true, "confidence": 0.92, "intent_a": "...", "intent_b": "..." }
```

The existing `StatementSignature::with_semantic_terms` in
`rust/src/summarization/dedup.rs` and the `RouteIntent` logic in
`rust/src/capability_routing/` are good starting points: they already group
semantically equivalent phrasings for tool routing and statement deduplication.
Extending that logic to the general two-prompt case would close this gap without
neural inference.

attempted.body:
## Summary

On 2026-10-20 Hive Mind 2.39.2 ran the three Hello World issues with Formal AI **0.354.1** as the model, one per client. **None succeeded:**

| Client | Issue / PR | Execution | Result | What Formal AI produced in this run |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code (`--tool claude`) | [Kotlin #1](https://github.com/konard/test-hello-world-019fb330-fa49-7c9d-a664-b7ea33bb698a/issues/1) / [PR #2](https://github.com/konard/test-hello-world-019fb330-fa49-7c9d-a664-b7ea33bb698a/pull/2) | `2719fb28` | **failed, exit 1** after 7 min 28 s | Session 1: correct `Main.kt`, verify script, compiled, ran, committed and pushed `139e03c`. Left `Main.jar` untracked. Session 2 (restart for `Main.jar`): an invalid `gh` command, then stopped |
| Codex (`--tool codex`) | [Rust #1](https://github.com/konard/test-hello-world-019fb331-c107-78c7-8ff6-9f127a3c593c/issues/1) / [PR #2](https://github.com/konard/test-hello-world-019fb331-c107-78c7-8ff6-9f127a3c593c/pull/2) | `b8b78e59` | **stopped by the operator, exit 137**, after 14 h 8 min | `main.rs` + verify script, compiled and ran, committed. **Pushed to branch `so`** (fails), then **210** `web_run` calls with `{}` until the sidecar was stopped. No workflow |
| Agent CLI (`--tool agent`) | [Scala #1](https://github.com/konard/test-hello-world-019fb330-00e1-73b9-955e-f357a1600d5b/issues/1) / [PR #2](https://github.com/konard/test-hello-world-019fb330-00e1-73b9-955e-f357a1600d5b/pull/2) | `2e56df93` | **failed, exit 1** after 2 h 39 min | Nothing new: 7 attempts, each repeated the same reads and writes and stopped at `scalac: not found` |

Goal of this issue: everything Formal AI must change so that the **next release completes all three runs**. Each item below has the evidence from these logs, the related issue if one exists, and a regression test built from this exact input. Parts outside Formal AI are listed at the end and tracked in their own repositories.

This continues #1162 (the same three tasks on 2026-09-27 with 0.352.1) and #1328 (the Codex loop of this run, observed live).

## What went wrong, per task

### 1. Claude Code, Kotlin (`2719fb28`, 14:14 → 14:21 UTC)

1. Session 1 (`858bf47a`, 7 turns) did the work correctly:
   - `gh issue view` (title and body);
   - wrote `Main.kt` and `tests/verify-output.sh`;
   - ran `kotlinc Main.kt -include-runtime -d Main.jar`, then the verify script (`Hello, World!`);
   - `git add … && git commit … && git push -q origin 'issue-1-604f2202fd18'` → `139e03c`, pushed.

   It ended `subtype=success` with "Created and verified `Main.kt` through the agentic CLI harness."
2. **`Main.jar` was left untracked** in the working tree: Formal AI's own build command writes it into the repository root. Hive Mind restarts the session for every uncommitted file (#1157 has the same symptom from 2026-09-27).
3. Session 2 (`539e9b34`, 2 turns) got Hive Mind's restart prompt, which lists `?? Main.jar` and asks to commit, ignore or delete each file. Formal AI did none of that. Its only step was:
   ```
   gh pr view 'https://github.com/…/pull/2' --comments --json comments,reviews
   → Exit code 1: specify only one of --comments or --json
   ```
   It then ended with "Prepared-work continuation stopped at `gh pr view …`". The usage error names the fix (`--json comments,reviews` alone), but Formal AI neither retried it nor moved on to the actual request (`Main.jar`).
4. Hive Mind then stopped with "no progress between sessions" (same HEAD `139e03c`, `Main.jar` still there), exit 1.

The PR content is close to complete: `Main.kt`, the verify script and `.github/workflows/run.yml` (from the 2026-09-27 run) are there, and CI passes. What failed the run is the build output and the second session.

### 2. Codex, Rust (`b8b78e59`, 08:27 → 22:36 UTC)

Details and the live observation are in #1328. Final numbers:

1. 08:41:50: `rustc main.rs -o main`, the verify script passed, and `git commit` succeeded. **`git push -q origin 'so'`** then failed with `error: src refspec so does not match any`. The branch name came from the system prompt's guideline sentence "commit each atomic step … to the pull request **branch so** interrupted work remains preserved". The real branch `issue-1-09b0c76bd0e4` appears 11 times in the same Codex session (`turn_context.git.branch`, the prompt).
2. 08:43:55 → 16:35:10: **210** `codex_apps search_service.web_run` calls, all with `arguments: {}`, all rejected (`InvalidActionArgumentsError … missing_required_argument`). Before every call the text was the same: "Let me search the web for rust src refspec so does not match any." There was no repeat stop. Each answer used 57–140 s of a full core, and the request body grew by 864 B per call.
3. After the sidecar was stopped (16:35:50), Codex waited "for network" until the operator stopped the task at 22:36. Hive Mind then auto-committed and pushed the untracked **`main` binary (4.5 MB)** that Formal AI's `rustc main.rs -o main` had left in the repository root (`693630a`). The same build-output problem as `Main.jar`.
4. **Requirement 6 (a GitHub Actions workflow) was never planned**: the PR has no workflow and no CI.

### 3. Agent CLI, Scala (`2e56df93`, 14:28 → 17:07 UTC)

1. Every attempt repeated the same steps: `gh issue view` ×2, write `Main.scala`, write `tests/verify-output.sh`, `scalac Main.scala` → `/bin/sh: 1: scalac: not found` (exit 127), then stop. There were 7 attempts: the first plus 6 Hive Mind retries of the same session; the last one failed at once on the stopped sidecar. `scalac` ran 8 times. **No commit was made on 2026-10-20**: the PR still has only the September commits.
2. Formal AI never checked which toolchain exists (`command -v scalac`, `scala-cli`, `cs`, `sbt`), never tried a fallback, and never handed compilation to CI (the PR already has a workflow that passes). #1159 is the same failure from 2026-09-15.
3. **The tool's exit code was misread.** The agent CLI's tool result carries `"metadata": {"exit": 127}` and `"error": "Exit code 127\n/bin/sh: 1: scalac: not found"`, yet Formal AI answered "Step `scalac Main.scala` for `Main.scala` failed. **No exit code was reported**, so the verdict rests on what the tool said".
4. A resumed session re-ran the steps the history already showed as done (see #1328, attempts 1–5).
5. 17:07: Hive Mind's retry found the stopped sidecar unreachable and failed the task properly ("the Formal AI endpoint … could not be reached").

### Sidecar, all three runs

- **Logs and memory not written.** During the Claude run alone there were 83 `level error` lines: `[dialog-log] failed to record exchange: Permission denied (os error 13)`, `logging_failed_check_log_directory_permissions_and_space`. There were also `[memory] failed to record live chat exchange: refusing to write an incompatible persisted-memory schema`. The permission part is Hive Mind's volume ownership (link-assistant/hive-mind#3583). **The incompatible persisted-memory schema is Formal AI's**: an existing memory volume from an older version can't be used, and nothing upgrades it (compare #982).
- **`formal-ai serve` ignores SIGTERM.** `docker stop -t 10` ended with exit 137 (#1328).
- **The runs used 0.354.1** although v0.355.0 had been released at 2026-10-19 22:37 UTC, about 10 h before the first run. Its notes mention "Preserve observed tool exit status …", "keep explicitly requested workflow paths in fetched coding tasks" and "Continue missing-command recovery …". So items 4, 6 and 7 below may be partly addressed already, but they are unverified for these inputs.

## What Formal AI must fix (each with a regression test from these logs)

1. **Branch name from the prompt's prose** (`so`). Push to the checked-out branch (`git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`, or the client's `git.branch` context), never to a word taken from guideline text. Test: the exact Codex system prompt and turn context from `b8b78e59` → `git push origin issue-1-09b0c76bd0e4`. (#1328)
2. **Tool calls with empty or invalid arguments, and no repeat stop.** `web_run` must get its `input`/`query`. The same failing call with the same arguments must not be planned again: after the second identical failure, change the plan or end the task with an honest failure. Test: the `b8b78e59` transcript at item 12 ends in ≤ 2 identical calls. (#1328)
3. **Build outputs left in the repository** (`Main.jar`, `main`). Build into a temporary directory, or add a matching `.gitignore` and commit it, or delete the output after verifying. Never leave an untracked file. Test: Kotlin and Rust tasks end with an empty `git status --porcelain`. (#1157)
4. **Hive Mind's continuation prompt.** When the prompt lists uncommitted files, handle each one as asked (commit, ignore or delete) before anything else. A usage error from `gh` (`specify only one of --comments or --json`) must be corrected and retried, or skipped, instead of ending the session. Reading PR feedback must use valid flags (`gh pr view <n> --json comments,reviews`). Test: the `539e9b34` input ends with `Main.jar` ignored or removed, pushed, and a clean tree. (#1158, #1157)
5. **Requirement coverage before success.** Check every numbered requirement of the issue before answering success. Here requirement 6 (a GitHub Actions workflow that builds and runs the program on push and pull request) was never planned for Rust, and for Kotlin and Scala it was never checked against the existing `run.yml`. Test: all three issue bodies → a workflow exists, runs the program and the verify script, and CI is green.
6. **Missing toolchain.** Probe before compiling (`command -v`). If the compiler is missing, use an available alternative or install it in user space (e.g. `scala-cli` / coursier for Scala). As a last resort, commit the source, verify script and workflow and let CI build it, with an honest note that local compilation was not possible. Never stop with the work uncommitted. Test: the Scala issue in an image without `scalac` → the work is committed and CI is green. (#1159)
7. **The agent CLI's tool-result format.** Read `state.metadata.exit` (and `state.error` "Exit code N") from OpenCode-style `tool_use` parts. "No exit code was reported" was false here. Test: the `scalac` result from `2e56df93`. (0.355.0 "Preserve observed tool exit status" may cover this; please confirm with this exact input.)
8. **Resumed sessions.** Continue from the last completed step instead of re-running finished reads, writes and commands. A resume after a completed, committed step should make no further changes. Test: resuming `ses_ea64805c8ffe…` after attempt 1 does not rewrite `Main.scala`. (#1157, #1328)
9. **Evidence files committed into the user's PR.** Both the Kotlin and Rust runs committed `dev/log/self-authored/issue-1/evidence/{claude,codex}-stream.jsonl` as **empty files (0 bytes)**, plus `session-id.txt`. Please decide: either commit them with content (and say so in the PR description), or keep them out of the user's repository. An empty evidence file proves nothing and adds noise to a Hello World PR.
10. **Persisted-memory schema.** Upgrade or migrate an older memory volume unattended and without data loss, or start a new one and say so. Don't refuse every write for the whole session. (#982)
11. **SIGTERM.** `formal-ai serve` should shut down within the stop timeout instead of being killed (exit 137). (#1328)

## Outside Formal AI (tracked in their own repositories)

- **link-assistant/agent:** its own `POST /session/<id>/message` request is reset after ~256 s (255,992 / 256,052 / 256,215 ms). With Formal AI at 60–140 s per step, every session longer than about 4 minutes hits it.
- **link-assistant/hive-mind:**
  - it takes that reset for a transient network failure and resumes the session (Retry 1–6, 3 → 30 min);
  - its `--auto-commit-uncommitted-changes` committed and pushed a 4.5 MB compiled binary;
  - the failed Kotlin run ends with PR #2 ready for review, not draft ("Converting PR: To ready for review (run end (No progress between sessions))");
  - the runs used 0.354.1 although 0.355.0 was out;
  - #3583 (volume ownership).
- **Codex 0.163.0:** with a local provider that is down it waits for the network indefinitely instead of failing the turn.

## Acceptance (the next release)

1. Each fix above has a regression test whose input is taken from these logs (prompts, transcripts, tool results), and the tests run in Formal AI's CI.
2. Against a local `formal-ai serve --agent-mode`, with Claude Code (Kotlin), Codex (Rust) and the Agent CLI (Scala) as clients, using **these three issue bodies and these PR branches**, each run ends with:
   - one program file printing exactly `Hello, World!` with explaining comments and build/run instructions;
   - a verify script and a workflow that runs both on push and pull request, with green CI;
   - no build outputs committed and a clean working tree;
   - everything pushed to the PR branch;
   - the PR description updated and the PR ready;
   - CLI exit 0.

   A second run on the same checkout is a no-op success. No run makes more than 2 identical failing tool calls.
3. Then Hive Mind's `/claude`, `/codex` and `/agent` runs of the same three issues all end with `✅` (exit 0) on the released image.

## Logs (secret gists; the email and Codex `account_id` are redacted)

- Claude Code / Kotlin, execution `2719fb28`, 14:14 → 14:21 UTC: https://gist.github.com/konard/bde1161e75014632ee711c07328f21b9
- Codex / Rust, execution `b8b78e59`, 08:27 → 22:36 UTC: https://gist.github.com/konard/fc014070fb8976cd3ad7766ed0675c0a
- Agent CLI / Scala, execution `2e56df93`, 14:28 → 17:07 UTC: https://gist.github.com/konard/74beb03d2d22bfaf8bb8b96dc6bd73e1
- Formal AI 0.354.1 sidecar stdout, 08:27 → 16:35 UTC: https://gist.github.com/konard/64cec5f80bec8275df4d255399a7e80e

Research & Implementation: Enhancing the Temperature and Randomization Mechanism via ProbabilityStore and Memory Dreaming
attempted.body:
### 1. Context & Theoretical Background
Following recent advancements in complexity theory (specifically the RL = L derandomization proof introduced in OpenAI's October 6, 2026 release), it is mathematically established that randomness does not grant additional computational power to bounded-memory algorithms. However, in engineering practice, incorporating controlled randomness (such as temperature) can significantly accelerate solution discovery, prevent local minima entrapment, and balance the trade-offs between strict deterministic exploration and heuristic acceleration.

As a symbolic, deterministic framework built on GOFAI traditions, Formal AI must reflect these principles realistically within its architecture, rather than mimicking LLM hyperparameter concepts on a surface level.

### 2. Current Implementation Analysis & Facts
Based on the current codebase audit:
* **Deterministic Core:** The codebase relies on `rust/src/solver.rs::UniversalSolver`, which executes a strict 11-step loop (from impulse formalization to solution composition) for every prompt.
* **Non-Neural Architecture:** Knowledge is represented as an inspectable semantic network of human-readable links instead of hidden weights.
* **Existing Infrastructure:** The system already defines a `ProbabilityStore` capable of handling append-only Bayesian evidence and Markov transitions.
* **The Policy Gap:** While `ProbabilityStore` ranks symbolic candidate IDs before the temperature/clarify-vs-guess policy runs, the temperature parameter currently has a minimal impact on the runtime complexity and search behavior of the deterministic solvers (`solver.rs` and `solver_unknown_reasoning.rs`). At `temperature = 0`, the system should guarantee high-quality deterministic results (even if it takes longer), while `temperature > 0` should enable accelerated heuristic shortcuts based on probabilistic evidence.

### 3. The Role of Memory Dreaming in Probabilistic Alignment
To make this system truly dynamic and adaptive, the background **`memory dream`** mechanism (tracked under issue #540) must act as the primary engine for updating `ProbabilityStore`. 

While the core server is idle, the dreaming worker should analyze the interaction history with the user and the environment to **increase the baseline probability of obtaining the most relevant answers**. Instead of real-time weight calculations during a hot chat turn, `memory dream` will:
* Aggregate and compress the append-only event log into long-term statistical trends.
* Update Bayesian evidence inside the link-network, prioritizing paths, contexts, and rules that have historically led to verified, high-quality outcomes.
* Mine recurring multi-turn task structures, dynamically updating Markov transition probabilities so that future heuristic searches (`temperature > 0`) lean toward proven contextual pathways.

### 4. Proposed Research Goals
We need to conduct a deep dive into our solver mechanics to make the randomization/temperature behavior realistic and functional:
1. **Define `temperature = 0` Execution Path:** Ensure that at zero temperature, the `UniversalSolver` falls back to complete, exhaustive symbolic path traversal, ensuring maximum precision and deterministic accuracy, accepting the higher time/step cost if necessary.
2. **Implement Probabilistic Acceleration (`temperature > 0`):** Use the `ProbabilityStore` Markov transition weights to greedily prune or prioritize search paths within the link network, mimicking how higher temperature values allow algorithms to jump out of local minima or bypass exhaustive checking.
3. **Bridge Dreaming and ProbabilityStore:** Formally map the output of background `memory dream` analysis onto the active weights of the `ProbabilityStore`.
4. **Verify Contract Stability:** Ensure that enabling/disabling randomness or modifying temperature does not degrade the core symbolic verification pipelines pinned by our regression suites (e.g., HumanEval/MBPP controls, egg rewrite laws).

### 5. Regression Control (`docs_benchmarks.rs`)
To prevent future regressions and enforce the strict operational semantics of temperature settings, we must implement a dedicated unit/integration test within `rust/tests/unit/docs_benchmarks.rs`. This test will:
* Assert that a set of highly connected link subgraphs evaluated at `temperature = 0` successfully traverses all possible branches, returning exact results while validating the step/time cost.
* Assert that the same subgraph evaluated at `temperature > 0` with populated `ProbabilityStore` weights achieves a lower total step count (heuristic acceleration) without violating baseline correctness.
* Ensure any deviation from these committed architectural ledger entries causes a test failure (`rust/tests/unit/docs_benchmarks.rs` enforcement).

### 6. Proposed Action Plan
* Audit `rust/src/solver.rs`, `rust/src/solver_unknown_reasoning.rs`, and the background dreaming worker to map out exact integration points for `ProbabilityStore`.
* Implement the new step-count validation test within `rust/tests/unit/docs_benchmarks.rs`.
* Document the findings and formalize the updated policy under `VISION.md` and `ARCHITECTURE.md`.

attempted.title: [Bug][P0] Work-item inspection stops before a useful edit: connect evidence, obligations, patch synthesis and independent checks
attempted.body:
**Type:** Bug · **Priority:** P0

## Problem and current evidence

The normal issue-to-draft path can inspect a work item but still cannot construct the requested change. This is the highest-priority capability gap for Formal AI participating in its own development.

In [issue #1455](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1455), the task named real dependencies and source files and requested a guide update. [Run 40721047258, job 122939497259](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/40721047258/job/122939497259) produced `planned_not_executed`; PR #1456 contained evidence and a marker rather than the requested implementation. The independent `gap-no-implementation` rejection was correct.

PR #1461 subsequently repaired the guide and added bounded repository evidence inspection. The [current handoff](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/528053940e8015d16752ee625cffcf15eedc0487/docs/case-studies/issue-1455/handoff.md) explicitly states that general evidence-to-edit synthesis, complete requirement binding and independent verification remain unfinished. This issue addresses that remaining generic capability; it does not reopen the already-fixed documentation omission.

Related owners: #1209, #1165, #1167, #1183 and #1170. Reuse the current work-item executor, obligation ledger, source representation, meta reasoner and repair loop.

## Outcome that unblocks development

Given an ordinary issue and a checkout, Formal AI produces at least one independently useful requested patch or regression test, with unresolved requirements explicit. A complete task is marked complete only after all mandatory obligations pass. Useful partial work remains available for later human/LLM review.

## Implementation steps

1. Make the production work-item controller carry one state throughout: task identity and source spans; typed obligations; observed facts and uncertainty; missing evidence; candidate edits; checks; executed effects; remaining work.
2. Discover only evidence needed to resolve a current obligation or choose between candidate edits. Start from referenced files, local symbols/tests/manifests and declared tools. Search primary documentation only when a concrete missing fact warrants it. Retain source/version/applicability and contradictions; fetched text is evidence, not authority to change the goal.
3. Treat image-only attachments and unavailable reads as explicit unresolved evidence. The screenshot-only Hive #3863 is an intake/diagnosis case, not a clean text synthesis benchmark. OCR or structured extraction may supply fallible observations; do not invent attachment contents.
4. Decompose the task into the smallest useful checkable change. Use the existing recursive source/meta-language representation to propose a supported structural edit with preconditions, changed/preserved obligations, expected effect and provenance. Do not add handlers keyed to issue numbers, entire prompt strings or a known final patch.
5. Derive tests from the task contract before candidate selection where applicable. Locate existing acceptance tests and keep an independent checker outside the candidate's control. A self-generated test is evidence, not proof that the interpretation is correct.
6. Execute the candidate, inspect compiler/test/tool results, revise the failed assumption and retry within an explicit budget. Preserve actual exit status, client context and idempotent continuation. Reuse #1185/#1157/#1159 machinery.
7. Return concrete artifact/commit identities and per-obligation results. Plans, reads, logs, trailers and `.gitkeep` changes earn zero implementation credit. Legitimate requested documentation/configuration changes remain eligible.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Reproduce #1455 on its pre-fix checkout through ordinary Hive `solve --tool agent --model formal-ai`, with no completed solution supplied in the prompt or seed. The actual guide change is independently checked against manifests/source.
- [ ] Repeat on held-out variants with renamed paths, different components and one contradicted integration claim; reject unsupported claims instead of copying the request into documentation.
- [ ] Complete one small production logic repair and one useful regression-test task selected before execution. Include a task beyond the supported subset and retain an honest unresolved result.
- [ ] Execute the same controller through Claude and Codex client adapters with their ordinary Hive prompts. No LLM service participates in these Formal AI attempts.
- [ ] Re-running a completed task is verified no-op success; a first attempt with only diagnostic changes fails useful-change acceptance.
- [ ] Every accepted contribution has an independent requirement check, a concrete diff, and a recorded authorship boundary. Later agent help is visible and does not retroactively become Formal AI work.
- [ ] A small offline regression exercises the original failure and the state transitions; hosted native/client qualification is separate.

Start with a declared supported subset and useful partial contributions. Complete universal language understanding or full cross-language equivalence is not a prerequisite for the first useful patch.

## Dependency contract

**Blocked by:** none; this step can start independently.

**Blocks:** #1491, #1170.

Related umbrella issues provide context; their entire broader scope is not an implicit prerequisite.

attempted.title: [Bug][P0] Hive issue-created drafts run stale Formal AI: bind both selected sources to the actual serving runtime
attempted.body:
**Type:** Bug · **Priority:** P0

## Repository ownership

**Hive Mind implementation:** [link-assistant/hive-mind#3909](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3909). This Formal AI issue owns its caller/workflow integration and cross-repository acceptance. **Completion is blocked by that Hive Mind implementation.** Work on independent Formal AI changes can proceed in parallel.

## Problem and current evidence

Formal AI's issue workflow now builds current main, but Hive Mind's own issue-created draft path can still run the backend baked into an older image.

The [2026-10-30 Hive draft, run 41081977243/job 124153176671](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/41081977243/job/124153176671), for hive-mind#3863, reported wrapper and serving backend **0.355.15** around 15:41 UTC. [Formal AI v0.355.23](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/releases/tag/v0.355.23) had been published at 04:10:32 UTC that day.

At reviewed Hive source `279ac05609d2a791c184c4f9fe7ee071e40ef6a4`:
- [Dockerfile](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/279ac05609d2a791c184c4f9fe7ee071e40ef6a4/Dockerfile) defaults `FORMAL_AI_VERSION=0.355.15`.
- [formal-ai-draft.mjs](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/279ac05609d2a791c184c4f9fe7ee071e40ef6a4/scripts/formal-ai-draft.mjs) mounts a different binary only when explicitly supplied.
- [formal-ai-draft-image.lib.mjs](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/279ac05609d2a791c184c4f9fe7ee071e40ef6a4/scripts/formal-ai-draft-image.lib.mjs) permits fallback from the exact Hive image to `latest`.

The serving-version probe already exists. The missing guarantee is selection and custody of the intended runtime, not printing another version string. A one-time version bump only postpones the same defect.

## Outcome that unblocks development

Every live issue-created attempt measures the intended current Formal AI and Hive implementation. Historical replays remain pinned and explicitly historical.

## Implementation steps

1. Define a shared attempt identity containing Formal AI source SHA, Hive source SHA, package versions, binary digest, image digest, client/adapter versions and selection timestamp.
2. Resolve current sources once at live-attempt admission. Obtain authenticated artifacts for those exact sources, or build once when absent. Reuse the existing Formal AI caller-binary mount protocol and provenance checks.
3. Verify the actual process and serving endpoint match the selected artifacts before accepting work. Version equality alone is insufficient when different source commits share a version.
4. Apply this contract to both repositories' issue-open paths. Track the cross-repository change here and link the corresponding Hive PR; a Formal AI-only change cannot close the integration requirement.
5. Eliminate silent fallback to an unqualified image/backend. Unavailable artifacts produce a typed infrastructure/deferred outcome, preserving evidence and zero capability credit.
6. Distinguish live current-source evaluation, published-release qualification, and historical pinned replay in receipts and dashboards.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Build a Hive image, advance Formal AI, then open a new issue: the next live draft runs the newly selected Formal AI source without rebuilding the entire Hive base merely to update its backend.
- [ ] Compare selected source, authenticated binary/image identity and actual serving identity; mismatches are rejected before task effects.
- [ ] Missing exact images/artifacts cannot silently become `latest`.
- [ ] Current-source selection happens once per attempt and survives retries; a new source selection creates a new attempt identity.
- [ ] Both repositories demonstrate the same contract in issue-created workflows.
- [ ] Historical replay fixtures remain reproducible and cannot be reported as current-source success.
- [ ] Fast tests cover source drift and stale/missing artifact cases; one hosted attempt verifies the complete integration.

Related: #1210, #1162, #1364; Hive #2207/#2208 address older lifecycle/version-reporting concerns, which should not be reimplemented.

## Dependency contract

**Blocked by:** link-assistant/hive-mind#3909 for cross-repository completion.

**Blocks:** #1162.

Related umbrella issues provide context; their entire broader scope is not an implicit prerequisite.

attempted.body:
**Type:** Bug · **Priority:** P0

## Reproduction and current behavior

In [Original Hive run 40668396305](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/40668396305) on 2026-10-28, source authentication, build and image preparation passed. Claude delivered and passed [independent verification, job 122773758051](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/40668396305/job/122773758051).

[Agent job 122765110686](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/40668396305/job/122765110686) and [Codex job 122765110642](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/40668396305/job/122765110642) stopped **before client execution**: a required scheduled task-ladder run, `40675356715`, became pending after initial admission. Revalidation correctly refused execution. Downstream verification/persistence then failed because claim/result artifacts did not exist.

The current [hive-delivery-attempt.mjs](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/528053940e8015d16752ee625cffcf15eedc0487/scripts/hive-delivery-attempt.mjs) asserts fresh admission before producing a distinct deferred receipt. This is an orchestration gap; the unstarted clients are not evidence of reasoning failure.

## Outcome that unblocks development

A candidate can wait for real prerequisites and resume safely, with every client outcome represented. Required CI remains required.

## Implementation steps

1. Add explicit pre-effect states: eligible, deferred on named prerequisites, refused, claimed/running, completed, and interrupted/unknown-after-effects.
2. Persist a `deferred-before-effects` receipt before leaving an unclaimed client leg. Include exact source/attempt/client, prerequisite run IDs and statuses, timestamp and proof that no task effects were claimed.
3. Make verification, persistence and aggregation consume this typed outcome rather than trying to download nonexistent claim/result artifacts.
4. Resume or re-admit only when prerequisites for the same immutable candidate settle successfully. Respect effect ownership: never re-execute an already claimed leg just because a sibling was deferred.
5. If a prerequisite fails or the selected source changes, emit refusal or a new attempt identity. Do not mutate old failed receipts into successful ones.
6. Reuse existing claim, custody, protected-reference and cleanup controls. Avoid an unbounded sleep loop occupying a runner; use bounded rechecks and event-driven continuation where possible.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Replay the exact sequence: admission green; image prepared; required scheduled CI starts; two clients have not yet claimed effects.
- [ ] Those clients do not run, receive zero execution credit, and leave valid deferred receipts naming the blocking run.
- [ ] Downstream jobs report deferral without a cascade of missing-artifact exceptions.
- [ ] Once prerequisites pass, only unclaimed clients execute; a completed sibling is not duplicated.
- [ ] Failed prerequisites, changed source, ambiguous prior effects and duplicate delivery events are covered by negative tests.
- [ ] One fresh hosted three-client attempt, including verified no-op repeats and independent assertions, finishes with truthful per-client results.
- [ ] No pending, skipped or cancelled prerequisite is reclassified as passing.

Related: #1162/#1364 and Hive #3630. This issue does not weaken admission policy.

## Dependency contract

**Blocked by:** none; this step can start independently.

**Blocks:** #1490, #1162.

attempted.body:
**Type:** Feature · **Priority:** P0

## Evidence and scope

The successful [2026-10-27 Codex job 122104863176](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/40475832633/job/122104863176) downloaded an **8,478,177,064-byte** same-source Hive artifact from approximately 09:16:22 to 09:47:43 UTC (~31m21s), then loaded/validated it. The actual task ran approximately 09:54:11–10:00:20 (~6m09s).

Current [build-hive-original-delivery-image.mjs](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/528053940e8015d16752ee625cffcf15eedc0487/scripts/build-hive-original-delivery-image.mjs) exports a full `docker save | gzip -1` image. The delivery matrix downloads/loads it in each client leg.

Separately, [hive-mind-draft.yml](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/528053940e8015d16752ee625cffcf15eedc0487/.github/workflows/hive-mind-draft.yml) resolves current main and compiles a release binary per issue; its concurrency key includes issue number. This is a focused extension of #1191 and #1210. The JavaScript-first PR profile and docs-only filtering already exist; do not rebuild that policy from scratch or treat skipped heavyweight checks as execution evidence.

## Outcome that unblocks development

A developer receives a useful failure signal before waiting for a release or a full client matrix. Multiple issue attempts reuse one authenticated build for the same effective inputs.

## Implementation steps

1. Instrument queue, checkout, install, compilation, image preparation/transfer/load, solver, verification and publication time separately. Record transferred bytes and useful-attempt counts.
2. Extract small deterministic replay tests from real issue/client failures. Run the relevant JS behavior, schema, workflow-policy and cross-runtime contract checks before expensive work. Keep a maintained mapping from changed components/failure families to their focused tests.
3. Build Formal AI once per source/toolchain/target/features/lockfile identity. Authenticate the producer and digest; concurrent consumers share or await that artifact. Failed or mismatched builds are not reused.
4. Separate stable Hive base layers from the changing Formal AI binary and adapters. Use immutable digest-addressed layers or an equivalently authenticated incremental transport. Preserve same-source runtime custody; never replace the exact candidate with an arbitrary cached image.
5. Evaluate sequential client execution on one prepared runner versus parallel clients with layer reuse using measured wall time, cost and isolation. Pick the faster reliable arrangement from data.
6. Keep full native/client/release qualification at its proper boundary. The fast lane provides early feedback, not production-delivery credit.
7. Publish before/after measurements on comparable tasks, including cold and warm cache cases. Set numeric service-level targets from that baseline, then fail or alert on sustained regression.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Opening multiple eligible issues at the same source causes at most one binary production for the same effective build identity.
- [ ] All consumers verify exact producer/source/digest/target identity; stale, poisoned or incomplete artifacts are rejected.
- [ ] The three-client matrix no longer independently transfers the same multi-gigabyte base through Actions artifacts for every leg.
- [ ] A captured planner/adapter failure is caught by a small offline test without Docker, a release or full Rust compilation.
- [ ] A same-source warm attempt shows a measured reduction in time to first useful result and total transferred bytes; report cold-start tradeoffs too.
- [ ] Full original oracles, native qualification and publication checks remain intact.
- [ ] Per-issue logs and outcomes stay distinct despite shared build products.

attempted.title: [Bug][P0] Semantic identity loses operand order and logical connectives: preserve task meaning before planning or proving
attempted.body:
**Type:** Bug · **Priority:** P0

## Reproducible problem

Read-only JavaScript probes at Formal AI `528053940e8015d16752ee625cffcf15eedc0487` found:

| Input pair / request | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| `1 is less than 2.` versus `2 is less than 1.` | `restates` returned true; the reversed statement could be removed as a duplicate |
| `The program returns true or false.` versus `The program returns true and false.` | Same statement identity |
| `Prove there are not infinitely many primes.` through the worker | `proof_outcome: proven` while the returned argument proves the positive infinitely-many-primes proposition |

The final case is wrong proposition binding, not a valid proof of a false theorem.

Inspect [text_formalization.mjs](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/528053940e8015d16752ee625cffcf15eedc0487/js/agentic/crate/text_formalization.mjs), [dependency_summarization.mjs](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/528053940e8015d16752ee625cffcf15eedc0487/js/agentic/crate/dependency_summarization.mjs), and [formal_ai_worker_calendar_and_proofs.js](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/528053940e8015d16752ee625cffcf15eedc0487/js/worker/formal_ai_worker_calendar_and_proofs.js). Typed obligation/dialogue/quantity components already exist; this issue is about unsafe shared identity/dispatch fallbacks and their production callers.

## Why it blocks coding

An executor cannot correctly synthesize `a < b`, preserve a negated condition, distinguish one output from two, or verify the requested behavior if different propositions collapse before planning. More passing generated tests would then reinforce the wrong interpretation.

Related: #1166 obligation formalization, #1330 sameMeaning, #1156 output cardinality.

## Implementation steps

1. Preserve ordered semantic roles, literal values/types, polarity, conjunction/disjunction, quantifiers and scope in the supported typed representation. Unsupported structure must remain unresolved rather than being silently omitted from identity.
2. Separate candidate retrieval/similarity from checked equivalence and entailment. A bag/set of recognized terms may retrieve a candidate; it cannot certify that two statements mean the same thing.
3. Bind each task-critical proposition to original source spans and each proof/check to the exact proposition identifier, assumptions and result. Positive theorem recognition must not answer a negated request.
4. Audit deduplication, summarization, request routing, task formalization and proof selection for callers that promote lexical overlap into equivalence.
5. Keep observational tests, checked proof and unresolved interpretation distinct in machine-readable results.
6. Reuse existing parsers/typed semantics and shared cross-runtime fixtures; do not grow a list of special cases for these sentences.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The two ordered-comparison statements and the conjunction/disjunction pair remain distinct and are not deduplicated.
- [ ] A negated theorem request never receives success for the positive theorem. Return an appropriate counterexample/refutation or honest unsupported result with the request binding intact.
- [ ] Positive paraphrases in the supported subset still unify when a checked interpretation justifies it.
- [ ] New tests cover `a-b` versus `b-a`, `<` versus `<=`, `and` versus `or`, negation scope, and repeated mention versus an explicit instruction to perform an effect twice.
- [ ] Coding acceptance demonstrates that these distinctions survive issue text → obligation graph → candidate patch → independent test.
- [ ] Unrecognized grammar keeps unresolved obligations; it cannot yield an empty but supposedly proved specification.
- [ ] JS/TS and native implementations agree on shared fixtures, with native verification in CI.

This is a finite soundness repair for supported semantics, not a requirement to solve unrestricted natural-language understanding before useful coding can begin.

## Minimal local JavaScript probe

Run from the repository root (no native build or network required):

```js
import { WorkerHost } from './js/server/worker-host.mjs';
import { installNodeHost } from './js/agentic/node-host.mjs';
import { formalizeText, statementIdentity } from './js/agentic/crate/text_formalization.mjs';
import { restates } from './js/agentic/crate/dependency_summarization.mjs';
const worker = new WorkerHost();
await installNodeHost(worker);
const [a] = formalizeText('1 is less than 2.', 'en');
const [b] = formalizeText('2 is less than 1.', 'en');
console.log(restates(b, a)); // currently true
const [c] = formalizeText('The program returns true or false.', 'en');
const [d] = formalizeText('The program returns true and false.', 'en');
console.log(statementIdentity(c) === statementIdentity(d)); // currently true
const answer = await worker.solve('Prove there are not infinitely many primes.');
console.log(answer.intent, answer.evidence); // currently proof_request / proof_outcome:proven
```

The ordered-comparison statement IDs themselves differ; the unsafe term-set entailment fallback still makes `restates` return true. Preserve that distinction when locating the fix.

attempted.body:
**Type:** Feature · **Priority:** P1

## Goal

Measure the user's intended progress: a growing fraction of initial Formal AI work survives into accepted changes, with later review improving it rather than replacing everything.

This extends #1170 and #1219. Reuse existing provenance and mixed-authorship support; do not require an entirely autonomous PR before crediting a valid contribution.

## Current boundary

[scripts/self-hosting-metric.rs](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/528053940e8015d16752ee625cffcf15eedc0487/scripts/self-hosting-metric.rs) and attribution code count eligible attributed additions/deletions. Commit churn alone does not establish usefulness or retention into the reviewed result.

The existing [full verifier](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/528053940e8015d16752ee625cffcf15eedc0487/js/provenance/full-verifier.mjs) already authenticates Git effects, clean checkout and fresh pinned replay. It explicitly leaves `taskCorrectness: requires-independent-task-oracle` and `autonomousAuthorship: not-established`. Build on this distinction. Existing mixed-authorship tests already permit Formal AI and later authors in one PR.

## Implementation steps

1. Capture immutable base, first Formal AI candidate, later reviewed candidate, and merged result. Bind task, tests, source/runtime identity, tool evidence and assistance supplied to each.
2. Define contribution units tied to a requirement, regression test or source transformation. Track additions and deletions; avoid counting every intermediate edit as fresh contribution.
3. Record disposition: retained unchanged, retained through a justified transformation, replaced, rejected or uncertain. Renaming/formatting should not automatically destroy valid credit; unsupported semantic-equivalence claims must stay uncertain.
4. Use independent acceptance to determine usefulness. Include legitimate documentation/configuration and behavior-preserving refactors when their intended benefit is specified and checked, but report those task classes separately from algorithmic code repair.
5. Report: task success before review; tasks with at least one retained useful contribution; useful candidate units retained / useful candidate units proposed; final useful units attributable to Formal AI / total final useful units; reviewer corrections; and secondary text/AST survival. Publish denominators, exclusions and uncertainty.
6. Preserve the existing metric for historical continuity and introduce a versioned new series. Do not relabel old evidence as if the new measurement had existed.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Valid unchanged patch; renamed/reformatted useful patch; useful deletion; specified refactor; independently valuable regression test.
- [ ] Whole-patch replacement, reverted patch, repeated line churn, log/marker padding and generated-mirror duplication receive no inflated credit.
- [ ] Executing a supplied complete literal solution receives automation credit only, not autonomous problem-solving credit.
- [ ] An LLM reviewer's assertion cannot by itself establish formal equivalence or authorship.
- [ ] A mixed PR can earn partial verified credit without claiming the whole task was solved unaided.
- [ ] An actual reviewed development PR demonstrates the report, including unresolved attribution where appropriate.
- [ ] The dashboard distinguishes zero useful work, absent evidence and uncertain retention.

Measurement can start immediately and report zero honestly. It must not wait for a perfect general semantic-equivalence engine.

attempted.title: Agent mode 0.355.27 misroutes common file requests: typo 'corrent' becomes a path, 'delete all files' and 'search for TODO' run ls, 'how many files' runs pwd, shell lines pass through verbatim
attempted.body:
## Summary

Found while building the experimental `--use-formal-ai` mode of start (link-foundation/start#255, PR link-foundation/start#256). In that mode, start sends a natural-language request to Formal AI's OpenAI-compatible agent endpoint and runs the `bash` tool calls it returns, without a shell and under an effect policy.

With **Formal AI 0.355.27** (commit `4d57ec7b`, `node js/server/main.mjs --agent-mode`, Node.js v26.13.0), several common requests are routed to the wrong tool call. start reports the real outcome, so nothing unsafe happens, but the tasks are not done.

## Reproduction

```sh
H=$(mktemp -d)
HOME=$H FORMAL_AI_MEMORY_PATH=$H/m.lino node js/server/main.mjs --agent-mode --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18080 --silent &
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:18080/api/openai/v1/chat/completions -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "formal-ai",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "print list of files in corrent directory"}],
  "tools": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "bash", "description": "Run a shell command",
    "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"command": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["command"]}}}]
}'
```

For the second turn, send the assistant message back with a `tool` message such as `<untrusted_context>\nCommand: ls\nDirectory: /tmp/x\nOutput: a.txt\nb.txt\nError: (none)\nExit Code: 0\n</untrusted_context>`.

## Observed tool calls

| Request | Tool call returned | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `print list of files in current directory` | `ls` | `ls` ✅ |
| `print list of files in corrent directory` (typo from the start issue) | `ls 'corrent'`, which exits 2 | `ls`. The typo should be recognized as "current", not taken as a path. |
| `delete all files` | `ls`. The second turn is `finish_reason: stop` with "The `ls` command completed. Output: …" | Either the requested deletion (subject to the caller's policy) or an explicit "not supported". A listing should not end the turn as if the task were done. |
| `search for TODO in all files` | `ls` | `grep -rn TODO .` |
| `how many files are in the current directory` | `pwd`. The second turn says "The `pwd` command completed" and quotes the result but gives no count. | A listing followed by a count. |
| `show the first 5 lines of README.md` | `cat README.md` | `head -n 5 README.md` |
| `ls; rm -rf ~` | `ls; rm -rf ~` (the request text passed through verbatim) | The request should not be forwarded unmodified as a shell line. start refuses it (it never uses a shell), but other agent hosts might run it. |

## Impact on start

start reports the real status: for example, `the last tool call exited with 2` for the typo, and `finished after 1 tool call(s); no file changed` for `delete all files`. These requests therefore fail visibly rather than silently. The start documentation lists them as known limits of Formal AI 0.355.27.

This report was prepared by an AI solver (Claude) working on link-foundation/start#255.

attempted.title: JS HTTP agent mode eagerly initializes Rust grammar for simple listing; WASM-disabled host returns HTTP 500
attempted.body:
Reproduced while qualifying released `start-command@0.41.0` (link-foundation/start#256) against Formal AI `0.355.28`, source `df939f759123335d81b4d6e56ce59b0fa06b5597`, on Node.js `24.18.0`.

Scope: the local workflow explicitly prohibits Rust/product or Rust-grammar WASM execution. A test-only Node preloader traps WebAssembly compilation/instantiation. This is a qualified failure under that restriction, not a claim that unrestricted start is broken. The checkout reports dirty due to unrelated untracked files; no maintained source was edited for the probe.

Request: `print list of files in current directory` through the released `--use-formal-ai` CLI, with a private tiny fixture, 384 MiB server heap, 20-second task budget, zero retries and automatic issue/log uploads disabled. It exits 70 before any tool executes; all fixture files remain unchanged. A direct replay of the same first HTTP request returns:

```json
{"error":{"message":"Aborted(Error: LocalProductWasmForbidden). Build with -sASSERTIONS for more info.","type":"formal_ai_error"}}
```

The trapped initialization stack, with host paths removed, is:

```text
js/vendor/tree-sitter/web-tree-sitter.mjs: instantiateArrayBuffer / Parser.init
scripts/lib/source-cst-frontends.mjs: sourceCstFrontends
js/server/source-usage-rust-frontend.mjs: installSourceUsageRustFrontend
js/agentic/node-host.mjs: installNodeHost
```

`js/server/node-host-install.mjs` defaults `sourceUsageRustGrammar` to true, whereas the direct JavaScript host can be installed with false and already handles this class of request. Basic listing should not require initializing a Rust source parser.

Requested outcome:

- Lazily initialize Rust parsing only for an operation requiring it, or expose a trusted caller-owned JS-server capability option that disables the Rust frontend. Conversation/file contents must never grant capabilities.
- Keep simple filesystem tasks and supported JavaScript literal edits usable without Rust grammar/WASM. If a requested Rust operation needs an unavailable frontend, return a truthful typed unresolved capability result rather than HTTP 500 or a fabricated parse.
- Add an offline JavaScript regression with a WASM trap for the original listing and a small JavaScript edit. Retain full Rust/source-usage qualification in CI; do not compile or run Rust tests locally.
- Preserve immutable host-policy conflict checks and Rust/JavaScript behavior where the capability is available.

No raw local logs, environment, personal files, absolute host paths or credentials are attached. The previous direct JavaScript host remains the local fallback while this is unresolved.
